newsitem.title: Italy: Italy PM to visit Albania before security mission. [CORRECTED 08:45 GMT 13/4]
newsitem.headline: Italy PM to visit Albania before security mission. [CORRECTED 08:45 GMT 13/4]

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi will visit Albania on Sunday (corrects from Monday), two days before the bulk of an Italian-led multinational security mission starts arriving in the Balkan state.

A spokesman for Prodi said on Saturday that the prime minister would visit for one day but gave no further details. Prodi said earlier that Italy would begin deploying the main body of its 2,500-strong troop contingent to Albania from Tuesday.
The Italian troops will form the backbone of a 6,000-strong multinational force which has been sanctioned by the United Nations Security Council.
Their mission is to protect the delivery of aid supplies to Albania, where local media put the death toll from six weeks of unrest at 279.
U.N. Secretary General Koffi Annan, who is in Italy on official business, said on Saturday he believed the mission was crucial.

"To the soldiers about to go, I want to say that they have a difficult task ahead of them but one of great importance and honour," Annan told a news conference. "It is our duty to aid a neighbour who is in trouble.
"I am sure that they have the ability to defend their mandate, which is humanitarian, and themselves," he added.
Albania plunged into near-anarchy last month amid popular anger over the collapse of get-rich-quick investment schemes.
Violence broke out in the south after rebels looted army and police arms depots. The multinational force, the first of its kind to be led by Italy, has no mandate to disarm them.
The troops plan to secure Durres and the southern port of Vlore, the latter controlled by rebels, as well as Tirana airport and transport routes to protect food and medical aid.

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) said in a statement that a first aid shipment had left the Italian port of Trieste with some 400 tonnes of food aid destined for Durres. It was due to arrive on Tuesday morning.

Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta and Defence Chief of Staff Guido Venturoni, who has overall command of the mission, flew to Tirana on Saturday to meet Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino for talks ahead of the deployment.

Troops from France, Greece, Spain, Turkey and Romania are also in the force, which is being organised by a so-called coalition of willing nations. Austria and Denmark are also considering participation.
A French naval vessel with around 120 men aboard was expected to leave the Italian port of Brindisi this weekend for a reconnaisance mission in Durres.
"We are waiting for our orders to depart and go to Durres," said French Major Herve Gourmelon. "I would like to know the date as well. It could be this evening or tomorrow," he added.
Two Spanish naval ships were due to arrive in Brindisi on Sunday.

Prodi, who won parliamentary backing for the mission on Wednesday at the cost of a split with his hard-left allies, said he hoped "elections (in Albania) will happen quickly and that one month after the vote we can begin to bring our troops back".
The wave of unrest has forced Albanian President Sali Berisha to call a general election by the end of June.
